thread:
nina: Hey folks — flying into CDG late (23:45) with a 7h connection before a morning train. Anyone done overnight at Terminal 2? Best quiet corners / plug spots? Also curious about decent 1-2h showers.
samir: T2E has lots of seating near gates 50-60, usually quieter. Lots of outlets around the seating clusters.
kevin: If you have Priority Pass, the Air France lounges in T2G open late and have showers (sometimes they charge). Otherwise check "Mama Shelter" shuttle for lounges.
louise: Airport showers = lifesaver. Theres a pay-per-shower place near T2F last time I checked. Book on the app if possible.
terminalbot: Reminder: security re-clear may be required between some T2 sub-terminals. Allow 45min for transfers at night.
nina: Any luggage storage recs? Don't want to lug a big duffel if I'm trying to sleep.
samir: Left luggage in T2 has lockers but sizes vary. If you can, consolidate to a daypack and gate-check the big bag.
kevin: Pro tip: pick a bench near a wall, under a row of lights so you can put a hoodie over your face. Set multiple alarms.
louise: For snacks: avoid anything too greasy if you plan to nap. Nuts, sandwich, electrolyte sachets. Also tap water is fine to refill.
nina: Noise-cancelling buds vs earplugs — which is better for dozing?
samir: Earplugs + a cheap foam mask wins for short naps. ANC buds help if you're trying to actually sleep and tune out announcements.
kevin: Bring a short USB-C cable. Lots of charging stations are USB-A only, but some outlets are USB-C. A tiny adapter helps.
terminalbot: Useful link: https://www.parisaeroport.fr/en/passengers/shops-and-services/rest-and-refresh
nina: Amazing, packing a scarf, eye mask, plus a 20k powerbank. If anyone has a spare lounge guest pass, I will trade with pastries :wink:
louise: I have a one-time guest voucher from a hotel program I don't need. DM me and we can sort timings.
kevin: Safe travels! Ping when you land and we'll drop any last-minute tips.
